about: Why Shouldn't I Keep It is a two-panel still of Ian Holm as Bilbo Baggins, filmed from below as he fingers the One Ring in his hand. In the top frame he smiles fondly at it; in the bottom his face sets into a stubborn, sulky pout, as if talking himself into it. The scene is a small, very relatable moment of rationalization: he knows he should let go, and he is building the argument for why he will not. As a meme it captures anyone justifying keeping something they really should give up, from an item borrowed months ago to a bad habit.
origin: The frames come from Fellowship of the Ring (2001), the first film in Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy. Before leaving Bag End, Bilbo is supposed to leave the Ring to Frodo and stalls, muttering “After all, why not? Why shouldn't I keep it?”
usage:
The classic version uses his lines directly: top box “after all... why not?” and bottom box “why shouldn't I keep it?” For a custom joke, label the top box with the thing being kept and let the bottom reuse his line, or rewrite both lines as a two-step excuse.

It lands best on harmless greed: the friend's hoodie, the office stapler, the extra fries, a free trial you forgot to cancel. The smile-to-pout shift reads as the moment of rationalization, so put the weaker excuse in the bottom line.
